evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/api/HttpClientProvider.kt:37-43 — HttpClient { install(ContentNegotiation) { json(json) }; install(Logging) { level = LogLevel.NONE }; defaultRequest { contentType(...) } }. No HttpTimeout plugin is installed and grep 'HttpTimeout' across mobile-native/ returns zero matches. Ktor 3.x does NOT install HttpTimeout by default; without it, request/connect/socket timeouts fall through to platform defaults (effectively unbounded on a hung TCP connection).

Every repository shares this client — ApiClient.kt:32, ListingRepository.kt:18, FavoritesRepository.kt:18, InquiryRepository.kt:18, NotificationRepository.kt:18, PortalListingsRepository.kt:25, AgencyRepository.kt:20, RealtorRepository.kt:20, SsoService.kt:25 — so a stalled server leaves every screen's spinner spinning forever with no CancellationException surfaced.
Fix: install(HttpTimeout) { requestTimeoutMillis = 30_000; connectTimeoutMillis = 10_000; socketTimeoutMillis = 30_000 } in HttpClientProvider.kt — one-line change covers the entire mobile fleet.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/account/ProfileStats.kt:42-45 — load() runs three independent suspend calls sequentially: favoritesRepository.getFavorites(), favoritesRepository.getSavedSearches(), inquiryRepository.getInquiries(). Each awaits the previous.

The three endpoints are independent; coroutineScope { async { ... }.awaitAll() } would fold latency to max() instead of sum(). On a 500 ms P95 backend round-trip this is 1.5 s vs 500 ms on the Account screen open.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/reports/mod.rs — four report handlers swallow repository DB errors with .unwrap_or_default() and serve HTTP 200 with silently-zeroed/empty data. Intra-handler inconsistency: primary query uses .map_err(...)?, secondary queries in the SAME handler discard the Result.

get_fault_statistics_report: get_monthly_fault_counts (:633) and get_monthly_resolution_times (:640) — transient DB error yields empty monthly_counts / resolution_time_trend arrays; report shows zero faults over time while primary stats block is populated.
get_voting_participation_report: get_participation_report (:715) — DB error makes participation_data an empty Vec; total_votes computes to 0 and quorum/participation summary is silently wrong.

get_occupancy_report (:827) and year-over-year sibling (:844) — DB error produces defaulted OccupancyReport with total_person_months == 0; year-over-year change_percentage computed against zeroed totals.
get_consumption_report (:949) and detect_consumption_anomalies (:962) — DB error silently drops all consumption rows/anomalies; monitoring/billing report shows zero usage on partial backend failure.

Impact: manager-facing analytical reports (fault trends, voting quorum, occupancy, utility consumption) degrade to HTTP 200 with zeros on transient DB error rather than 5xx the caller can retry. Fix: replace .unwrap_or_default() with .map_err(...)? -> 500.
